🐳 Docker Architecture

WISC AI uses Docker Compose to orchestrate multiple services. Each service runs in its own container, enabling independent scaling and deployment.

📁
Project Structure
SMART_ACCOUNTER/ │ ├── WISC/ # Main ERP System (.NET 9) │ ├── WISC.API/ # Main API Gateway │ ├── WISC.Domain/ # Domain Entities │ ├── WISC.Infrastructure/ # Data Access │ ├── WISC.AI.Mind/ # AI Core (Frozen) │ └── WISC.sln │ ├── RAGClass/ # AI Command Layer │ ├── WISC.AI.Commands.Sql/ # SQL Generation │ ├── WISC.AI.Commands.Sql.Tests/ # Security Tests │ └── WISC.AI.Mind/ # AI Interfaces │ ├── WISC_DOCS/ # Documentation │ ├── WISC_LANDING.html │ ├── WISC_INTRO.html │ └── ... 🏗️ Microservices Structure

WISC AI follows a modular architecture where each component can run independently or as part of the complete system.

🎯
WISC.API

Main API Gateway - Entry point for all client requests. Handles authentication, rate limiting, and routes to AI services.

.NET 9 JWT Auth SignalR Rate Limiting
dotnet run --project WISC/WISC.API

Run independently on port 5000

🧠
WISC.AI.Mind

AI Core Layer - Frozen, immutable core containing SQL generation logic. Decorated by security and persona layers.

RAG Pipeline Decorator Pattern Strict Offline

🔒 FROZEN - Never modify directly

Extend via Decorators only

🛡️
WISC.AI.Commands.Sql

SQL Command Generation with Security. Validates tenant isolation and business rules before execution.

SQL Generation Security Guards Smart Tags
dotnet test WISC.AI.Commands.Sql.Tests

Run security tests independently

🗄️
WISC.Infrastructure

Data Access Layer - Entity Framework Core, Repository Pattern, Unit of Work.

EF Core 9 SQL Server SQLite
dotnet ef migrations add Initial

Database migrations

🎨
WISC-UI (Angular)

Web Frontend - Responsive Angular application with real-time SignalR integration.

Angular 17 TypeScript SignalR Client
ng serve --port 4200

Run independently (requires API)

🚀 Deployment Workflows

Local Development

1

Start Infrastructure

docker-compose up -d sqlserver ollama redis

Database and AI services start first (independent)

2

Run API Locally

dotnet run --project WISC/WISC.API

API runs outside Docker for debugging

3

Run Angular UI

cd WISC-UI && ng serve

Frontend hot-reload development

Production Deployment

1

Build All Images

docker-compose build

Builds API, Ollama, and Angular containers

2

Deploy Stack

docker-compose up -d

All services start together with proper dependency order

3

Verify Health

curl http://localhost:5000/api/health

Check all services are running

🔧 Running Services Independently

Each component can be developed and tested in isolation. This is the key benefit of microservices architecture.

🧪
Independent Development
Service Independent Command Dependencies
WISC API dotnet run WISC.API SQL Server, Ollama (optional)
AI Tests dotnet test WISC.AI.Commands.Sql.Tests None (mocked)
Angular UI ng serve API running on :5000
Ollama Only docker-compose up ollama None
Database Only docker-compose up sqlserver None

Key Benefits

  • Parallel Development: Teams work on different services simultaneously
  • Independent Testing: Unit tests for each module without full system
  • Selective Deployment: Update one service without affecting others
  • Technology Freedom: Each service uses best-fit technology (will be used for Python AI services)
  • Fault Isolation: Failure in one service doesn't crash the entire system
